primary_topics: BLD (Bukas Loob sa Diyos) testimony about applying Christian faith to civic work, August 25, 1995 -- shared at a BLD gathering; focus is on the Rotary Club Manila presidency (1990-1991)

CJP's pre-1986 life: angry young man; born poor, parents died during schooling; seeking fulfillment through wealth (four million dollars in two years, lost in 1982 Hong Kong stock market crash) -- 'the lavish life-style I enjoyed did not bring me peace -- it merely increased my appetite for more'
The 1986 turning point: Life in the Spirit Seminar; baptism in the Holy Spirit; proclamation of Jesus as Lord and Savior; BLD membership; 'I developed a hunger for Scriptures'

LOVE GOD SERVE MAN credo applied to RCM presidency: 76-page Program of Action, 178 projects, P90M budget (18x the previous P5M maximum); inaugural July 12, 1990; P5.5M raised in 30 minutes for earthquake victims
sub_topics: Opening prayer: 'Lord Jesus, I pray that I may know you more clearly, and love you more dearly, so I can imitate you more nearly and serve you more eagerly. Amen.'

Pre-conversion restlessness: St. Augustine -- 'our hearts are restless till they rest in God'; CJP tried to quiet restlessness through wealth, power, fame; 'I was an angry young man and I vowed to have my own generous slice of worldly wealth, power, and fame'

Pre-conversion poverty: 'born to poor parents who both died at a relatively early age before I could finish my schooling. I knew the depths of poverty, of sleeping on the cold sidewalks, of selling newspapers, of shining shoes and of peddling textbooks to my classmates'

The wealth failure: 'in the early eighties, I quickly earned over four million U.S. dollars from zero in just two years, only for this incredible wealth to vanish into thin air in the stock market crash of 1982 in Hongkong. The lavish life-style I enjoyed did not bring me peace -- it merely increased my appetite for more and more.'

1986 turning point: 'found Jesus Christ; when I was baptized in the Holy Spirit during a Life in the Spirit Seminar; when I proclaimed Jesus as my Lord and Savior; when I knew that my purpose in life is to obey and glorify Him; when I realized that though I was in the world, I did not belong to this world.'

BLD gifts: 'I developed a hunger for Scriptures. With the help of my brothers and sisters in the Bukas Loob sa Diyos Covenant Community, I developed the Holy Spirit's gifts of discernment, sharing, reflection, prayer and healing.'

Rotary Club Manila presidency: RCM organized June 1, 1919; oldest Rotary Club in Asia; 455 members; largest in Asia, largest in world outside US; CJP topped the voting with a record margin in RCM history
Discernment process: 'before the election, I subjected this possibility to reflection and daily prayer'; after election, the group prayed and asked the Lord what to do; answer came in Isaiah 42
LOVE GOD SERVE MAN credo: 'based on Mark 12:29-32, our Lord Jesus Christ summarized all the commandments: love God with all your heart, soul, mind, strength. Love your neighbor as yourself.'

Program of Action: '76-page Program of Action, describing in detail 178 projects and activities, complete with specific days and months during my one-year incumbency. The Program of Action called for a budget of 90 million pesos, an outlay that is 18 times the biggest budget of 5 million pesos that RCM had in the past.'

Inaugural address (July 12, 1990): 'This is the base, the most important component, the driving force of my vision for Manila Rotary. As your President, I vow to channel our major treasures, time and talent in helping our less fortunate brothers.'

Earthquake response: 'the members responded with contributions and pledges amounting to a massive P5.5 million in just 30 minutes, followed by another P660,000 telephoned the following day, in total nearly seven million pesos for earthquake victims'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered August 25, 1995 at a Bukas Loob sa Diyos (BLD) gathering -- two months before CJP's SC appointment -- this is his pre-judicial testimony on applying Christian faith to civic work, specifically his Rotary Club of Manila (RCM) presidency. Opening prayer: 'Lord Jesus, I pray that I may know you more clearly, and love you more dearly, so I can imitate you more nearly and serve you more eagerly.' He traces his pre-conversion arc: St. Augustine ('our hearts are restless till they rest in God'); his own path through academic honors and student leadership that 'did not satisfy my thirst for life and love, for peace and happiness'; then the pursuit of worldly wealth -- 'in the early eighties, I quickly earned over four million U.S. dollars from zero in just two years, only for this incredible wealth to vanish into thin air in the stock market crash of 1982 in Hongkong. The lavish life-style I enjoyed did not bring me peace -- it merely increased my appetite for more and more.' The 1986 turning point: Life in the Spirit Seminar; baptism in the Holy Spirit; proclamation of Jesus as Lord; BLD membership; 'I developed a hunger for Scriptures... gifts of discernment, sharing, reflection, prayer and healing.' His RCM presidency (organized June 1, 1919; oldest Rotary in Asia; 455 members; largest in Asia and the world except the US): he subjected the election to BLD discernment and prayer; won with a record margin; the Isaiah 42 confirmation; formulated the LOVE GOD SERVE MAN credo (from Mark 12:29-32); expanded it into a 76-page Program of Action with 178 projects, P90M budget (18x the previous P5M maximum). Inaugural address (July 12, 1990): 'I vow to channel our major treasures, time and talent in helping our less fortunate brothers.' At the first regular meeting, members contributed P5.5 million in 30 minutes for earthquake victims, followed by P660,000 the next day: 'I view this tremendous outpouring of support not merely as an answer to my call to LOVE GOD SERVE MAN but as a sign of His Providence when we discern and obey His will and step out in faith to proclaim it.'
